events.text: A thin yellow dog has followed you for three villages, waiting outside every inn.

effects.log: It never leaves your side again.
It eats, looks at you, and lets you go. Some dogs have their own roads.

events.text: A temple cat climbs into your lap during a sermon, turns three times, and declares you its property.

effects.log: The abbot says the cat has chosen. You carry it home in your sleeve.
It looks at you with deep contempt and chooses a monk instead.

events.text: A hawk chick has fallen from a cliff nest, alive and furious. Its parents are nowhere.

effects.log: Months of raw meat and scratched arms. It becomes the best hunter in the valley.

choices.text: Climb and return it to the nest

effects.log: The parents scream at you all the way up and down.

variants: A hawk chick lies at the foot of a cliff, fallen from its nest, alive and furious. There is no sign of its parents.

events.text: In the snow you find a silver fox caught in a hunter's trap. It watches you with eyes that are far too wise.

effects.log: It limps away, looks back once, and a week later it is sleeping on your doorstep.
You walk on. The fox's eyes follow you in your dreams.

events.text: A tiger cub, its mother killed by hunters, hides under a rock and hisses at the whole world.

ok.log: Three days of patience and dried meat. It follows you home. Your neighbours move.

fail.log: It bites you and escapes into the forest.

choices.text: Bring it to the mountain monks

effects.log: The monks raise it. Years later it guards their gate.

events.text: A white crane with a hurt wing stands in your rice field, too proud to ask for help.

effects.log: It heals and does not leave. Old people say cranes bring long life.
It flies, badly, away. You hope it makes it.

events.text: Your dog chases a thief down the street and brings back his trousers. The thief is still wearing them, briefly.

effects.log: The thief thanks you, confused, and becomes an honest porter.
They hang in your house as a warning to others.

events.text: Your dog is old now and sleeps in the sun most of the day, but still stands up every time you come home.

choices.text: Sit with it in the sun

effects.log: An afternoon of nothing. It is enough.
It sniffs every tree like it is the first time.

events.text: Your cat leaves a dead rat on your pillow as a gift. It watches to see if you appreciate it.

effects.log: It purrs for an hour. Next day, two rats.

choices.text: Explain that rats are not gifts

effects.log: It stares at you with pity for your ignorance.

events.text: Your cat walks into a sect's training hall and sits on the master's cushion. Nobody dares move it.

effects.log: The master laughs. You are invited to stay for tea.

choices.text: Let the cat hold the hall

effects.log: The disciples train around it for an hour. It is the most disciplined session of their lives.

events.text: Your hawk circles high over the hills, then dives. It comes back with something that is not a rabbit: a small jade token.

effects.log: It turns out to be a sect token worth a favour. (20 taels from a grateful sect)
The sect thanks you with a meal and a very curious look at your hawk.

events.text: Your hawk screams from the sky and will not stop circling the road ahead.

effects.log: Later you learn bandits were waiting on the first. Good bird.
Bandits. You get through, but your hawk looks at you as if you were stupid.

events.text: A village horse race: a bag of rice to the winner. Your horse is already pawing the ground.

ok.log: Nose first across the line. A bag of rice and a village of new friends.

fail.log: Second. Your horse sulks for a week.

effects.log: Your horse carries a very small, very happy champion.

events.text: Bandits on the road, too many to fight. Your horse's ears go flat and it looks back at you.

effects.log: Your horse runs like the wind. The bandits eat your dust.

ok.log: Mounted, you scatter them like chickens.

fail.log: They pull you down. Your horse drags you clear.

events.text: Your fox steals a magistrate's seal and hides it in your boot. The magistrate is searching the whole town.

effects.log: The magistrate never learns who took it. The fox looks very pleased with itself.
One very official letter to a very corrupt landlord. Then you return it.

events.text: At midnight your fox sits in the moonlight, and for a moment it has more than one tail.

effects.log: It looks at you, and you could swear it winks.
It bows back. Nothing is ever quite ordinary again.

events.text: Your tiger is grown now. Bandits in three counties have decided your road is not worth the trouble.

effects.log: The market clears. The vegetable seller gives you everything free, to be safe.
No wolves, no bandits, no tax collectors. The village loves it, mostly.

events.text: Your tiger has eaten the magistrate's prize goat. The magistrate is not amused.

effects.log: Twenty taels. The magistrate keeps his distance after that.

ok.log: He laughs and admits the goat was a menace.

events.text: Your crane dances in the courtyard at dawn, long legs and wide wings. Passers-by stop to watch.

effects.log: You look ridiculous. You feel wonderful.

choices.text: Copy its steps in your footwork

effects.log: The crane's balance becomes your balance.

events.text: Your companion has not come home for two days. You search every field and every alley.

ok.log: You find it stuck in a well, furious and fine.

fail.log: You find it at dawn, hurt but alive, and carry it home.

choices.text: Ask the whole village to help

effects.log: The children find it within an hour. They are very proud.

events.text: A cold night. Your companion sleeps pressed against you, warm and breathing slowly.

effects.log: You sleep better than you have in a year.
It listens better than most people.

events.text: At the horse fair, a young mare refuses every buyer until she sees you. The dealer shrugs.

effects.log: She has chosen. (−40 taels)
She neighs after you all down the road.
